article_title: Dopamine sites: India and the world are discovering the thrill of shopping without buying

tasks.prompt: What central question does the article explore through “dopamine sites” such as FoodNeverComes?
options: Whether the anticipation and ritual of buying can be rewarding even when no real purchase occurs
Whether artificial intelligence can deliver restaurant meals faster than human riders
Why consumers no longer enjoy browsing products online
How fake travel sites can replace all real holidays
tasks.correct_answer: Whether the anticipation and ritual of buying can be rewarding even when no real purchase occurs
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה בוחנת האם הציפייה, החיפוש וטקס ההזמנה עצמם מספקים תגמול, גם ללא קנייה או צריכה ממשית.

tasks.prompt: What happens after a user completes a fake order on FoodNeverComes?
options: Real food arrives without a bill.
The site simulates delivery, including a dummy AI-generated call, but no food exists.
The user receives a cash reward from a restaurant.
The order is automatically sent to a real delivery platform.
tasks.correct_answer: The site simulates delivery, including a dummy AI-generated call, but no food exists.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: האתר מדמה את חוויית המשלוח ואף יוצר שיחת AI פיקטיבית, אך בפועל לא הוזמן ולא נשלח מזון.

tasks.prompt: What does Ravi Dhar mean by “anticipatory utility”?
options: The financial value of returning unwanted products
The practical usefulness of planning meals in advance
The pleasure people gain from looking forward to consumption
The ability of an algorithm to predict delivery times
tasks.correct_answer: The pleasure people gain from looking forward to consumption
tasks.explanation_hebrew: anticipatory utility הוא הערך או העונג שמופקים מן הציפייה לצריכה עתידית, עוד לפני קבלת המוצר או החוויה.

tasks.prompt: In Kent Berridge's explanation, what is “incentive salience”?
options: The satisfaction felt after owning a desired object
A price discount that makes a product affordable
The habit of comparing several products objectively
The motivational pull that makes a tempting object or cue strongly wanted
tasks.correct_answer: The motivational pull that makes a tempting object or cue strongly wanted
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המונח מתאר את הכוח המוטיבציוני שמעניק לגירוי בולטות וגורם לנו לרצות לרדוף אחריו, גם אם ההנאה הסופית תהיה חלשה.

options: Wanting is the drive to pursue something; liking is the pleasure of having it.
Wanting applies only to food, while liking applies only to shopping.
Wanting is conscious, while liking is always unconscious.
Wanting and liking are identical processes controlled in exactly the same way.
tasks.correct_answer: Wanting is the drive to pursue something; liking is the pleasure of having it.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ברידג' מפריד בין הדחף להשיג דבר לבין ההנאה ממנו לאחר ההשגה; דופמין קשור בעיקר ל־wanting.

tasks.prompt: What does Dhar suggest by calling simulated shopping a possible “release valve”?
options: It could permanently eliminate all consumer desire.
It might provide a safer outlet for an urge without a real purchase.
It forces users to reveal their spending data.
It increases the pressure to buy expensive products immediately.
tasks.correct_answer: It might provide a safer outlet for an urge without a real purchase.
tasks.explanation_hebrew: release valve הוא דימוי למנגנון שמפחית לחץ; כאן הכוונה לכך שסימולציה עשויה לתת פורקן לדחף בלי לבצע קנייה אמיתית.

tasks.prompt: Give two pieces of evidence showing the scale or detail of FoodNeverComes.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין שני נתונים מספריים או מאפיינים מדויקים של האתר מן הכתבה.
expected_points: It attracted more than 2.7 million visitors after launching in June.
It offers 22 fake kitchens or cuisines.
It includes 327 dishes and 319 real recipes.
It provides fake prices, checkout and a fictional delivery experience.

tasks.prompt: Why do the experts disagree about whether dopamine sites reduce or reinforce compulsive consumption?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: התשובה צריכה להסביר את שני הכיוונים האפשריים ולהתייחס לחוסר בראיות אמפיריות או להבדלים בין משתמשים.
expected_points: Simulated consumption may satisfy or redirect the urge without spending money.
Repeating the ordering ritual may rehearse and strengthen the same addictive neural networks.
The novelty may wear off, limiting repeated use.
Evidence is still limited and the effect may depend on the individual.

tasks.prompt: Summarise how dopamine sites work and what the article says about the psychology behind them.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: הסיכום צריך לתאר את הסימולציה ללא צריכה אמיתית, להסביר את ההבחנה בין wanting ל־liking או את תפקיד הציפייה, ולהציג לפחות אי־ודאות אחת לגבי ההשפעה.
expected_points: The sites reproduce shopping, ordering or travel rituals without delivering a real product or experience.
Anticipation and reward cues can create wanting even when ownership or consumption is absent.
Dopamine is presented as a driver of motivation rather than simply a pleasure chemical.
Experts are unsure whether the sites provide harmless release or reinforce compulsive habits.

tasks.prompt: Using evidence from the article, assess whether dopamine sites are more likely to help users control consumption or strengthen unhealthy habits.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לנסח טענה מנומקת, להשתמש בלפחות שתי ראיות או עמדות מומחים מן הכתבה, להתייחס לטיעון הנגדי ולסיים במסקנה זהירה.
expected_points: Evidence for benefit includes avoiding payment or consumption and Dhar's comparison with effective simulated consumption in gaming.
Evidence for harm includes Lembke's concern that repeated rituals may reinforce addictive neural networks.
Berridge expects novelty to fade, while the founders' experiences suggest browsing itself can satisfy some users.
A strong conclusion should acknowledge that empirical evidence is not yet sufficient and effects may vary by person.
